editorial.headline: A Doctor’s Independent Practice, and Bali’s PMA Boundary
editorial.standfirst: Independent general medical care may be nationally foreign-open, but a foreign doctor cannot register a solo practice in Bali.
editorial.body:
For a foreign doctor considering Bali, the conclusion comes first: this activity cannot be registered there today as an independent solo practice. Bali records it as closed to foreign nationals. That is the local position even though the national entry is open to foreign investment and sets a foreign-ownership ceiling of 100%. A national ceiling describes the extent of foreign participation allowed nationally; it does not, by itself, create a registration route in Bali.

The activity is a focused professional practice. It covers general care and treatment for diseases, delivered independently by a doctor. In clear English, it is the independent practice of a doctor providing general medical care. The word “independently” does important work here: the care and treatment within scope are carried out by the doctor as an independent practitioner. That gives the activity a defined clinical character rather than making it a broad label for health-related enterprise.

Nationally, the record makes the activity available at Micro, Small, Medium and Large scales. That is a notably broad range of business scales, while the centre of the activity remains the same: a doctor independently providing general care and treatment. The record does not supply further detail on facilities, credentials, permits or operating steps, and those should not be inferred from either the ownership status or the scale categories.

Bali is where national openness stops being the whole story. Its status is TERTUTUP—closed—and the stated rationale is health law: a foreign doctor cannot open a solo practice. The provincial PMA rule recorded here is island-wide and permanent. Read together, these facts establish a firm local boundary, not a technical footnote. A 100% national ceiling allows full foreign ownership nationally; it does not override Bali’s recorded closure of this activity to a foreign doctor. For a founder assessing this route, the honest Bali answer is therefore no registration of this independent practice by a foreigner.
editorial.pullQuote: A 100% national ceiling allows full foreign ownership nationally; it does not create a Bali registration route.
